newsitem.title: CANADA: Manufacturers Life buys 28 percent stake in Altamira.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturers Life buys 28 percent stake in Altamira.

text.p: Manufacturers Life Insurance Co., Canada's biggest insurance company, said on Thursday that it has reached an agreement in principle to buy a 28 percent stake in mutual fund giant Altamira Management Ltd.
Toronto-based Manulife, which indirectly holds 30.5 percent of Altamira shares, is Canada's largest insurance company with nearly C$50 billion ($37 billion) in assets.
Altamira is the country's biggest no-load mutual fund with about C$6.2 billion ($4.5 billion) in mutual fund assets.

Manulife is acquiring the 28 percent stake currently held by Altamira's management group. It plans to make an offer for the rest of Altamira, including any remaining management group shares not tendered to the offer.
"Within the next week or so we should be making an offer to everybody else," Manulife Chief Executive Officer Dominic D'Alessandro, said in a telephone interview.
The price of the transaction was not disclosed, but Canadian newspapers have valued Altamira at between C$600 million ($444 million) and C$800 million ($592 million).
Altamira managers will receive a combination of cash and equity in the firm. The managers have agreed to use significant portions of the cash to buy units in Altamira funds, Manulife said.
Altamira Investment President Philip Armstrong said the deal gives Altamira shareholders the best of both worlds -- a "satisfactory" price and a continued equity position.
"Altamira will be able to continue our close relationship with Manulife while operating as a separate company, ensuring that our entrepreneurial culture is preserved," Armstrong said in a statement.
D'Alessandro said Altamira will enhance Manulife's own wealth management business. "We now have a vehicle for being involved in the mutual fund business in Canada in a major way," he said.
The deal is subject to final legal agreements and regulatory approvals.
